answer: The design leans on time-locked work history, published publicly on failure, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Written in a short declarative sentences register, it stays short. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. The shale holds work receipts rather than names, so the orchard of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Reaching the knoll of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
